extracted.intended_audience: federal and state wildlife managers, regulated parties (landowners, hunters), conservation organizations, attorneys, and other stakeholders affected by Endangered Species Act rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule amending 50 CFR part 17 to reinstate Endangered Species Act protections for the gray wolf (Canis lupus), designate critical habitat, add a section 4(d) special rule for Minnesota, and make related technical corrections to regulatory text. The rule implements a court order and explains scope, prohibitions, permits, reporting, and future rulemaking actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of ESA protections per court order
rubrics_metrics.description: To comply with the February 10, 2022 district court order, the Service must reinstate: threatened species status for gray wolf in Minnesota; endangered species status for gray wolf in all or portions of 44 U.S. States and Mexico; critical habitat for gray wolf in Minnesota and Michigan; and a section 4(d) rule for gray wolf in Minnesota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinstatement implements the court's order and corrects the CFR to reflect pre-delisting protections. The court order had legal effect immediately on February 10, 2022; the final rule takes effect November 3, 2023. Note: wolves in Montana, Idaho, Wyoming, the eastern third of Washington and Oregon, and north-central Utah (Northern Rocky Mountains) retain delisted status and are not affected by this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is effective November 3, 2023. However, the court order had legal effect immediately upon its filing on February 10, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule explains both the publication effective date and that the court order's legal effect pre-dates the final rule. Where court orders apply, agencies may implement regulatory changes to conform to judicial relief, and should state both the effective date and any retroactive legal effects arising from the court order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Procedure — waiver of prior notice and comment (5 U.S.C. 553(b) and (d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director determined, pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(b), that prior notice and opportunity for public comment are impractical and unnecessary, and pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(d) that the agency has good cause to make the rule effective upon publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency relies on the judicial mandate to justify bypassing ordinary notice-and-comment procedures for reinstatement and for certain insignificant technical revisions. Use of the good-cause exception should be clearly explained and tied to statutory authority and factual circumstances (here, to comply with a court order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical revisions — insignificance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule makes the following technical revisions to the section 4(d) rule at 50 CFR 17.40(d): (1) correcting the misspelling of 'Hoodoo Point'; (2) correcting the misspelling of 'the Duluth, Missabe and Iron Range Railroad'; (3) substituting a higher quality image of the map of regulatory zones; and (4) updating the contact information for providing notifications to the Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes are combined with the reinstatement on the basis that they are 'insignificant in nature and impact and inconsequential to the public.' Technical corrections that do not change regulatory effect may be promulgated without separate notice-and-comment if supported by a showing of insignificance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing format and CFR amendments (50 CFR 17.11 entries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §17.11(h) by adding two entries for 'Wolf, gray' in alphabetic order under Mammals in the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife, including columns for 'Common name', 'Scientific name', 'Where listed', 'Status', and 'Listing citations and applicable rules'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory amendments must follow the prescribed format for CFR lists (alphabetical placement, required columns, citations). The rule provides the exact language and geographic annotations to be placed in 50 CFR 17.11(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of regulatory zones in Minnesota (§17.40(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of these regulations, Minnesota is divided into five zones (Zones 1–5) with detailed metes-and-bounds descriptions (and an accompanying map) specifying the boundaries and area (square miles) of each zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise geographic delineation (by highways, county routes, townships, sections, meridians, etc.) is required when defining zones for application of special rules; include both textual metes-and-bounds and an illustrative map to minimize ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions — taking a gray wolf in Minnesota (§17.40(d)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, no person may take a gray wolf in Minnesota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text must state the prohibition clearly and then enumerate exceptions. Here prohibition is absolute except for specified exceptions (defense of life, designated agents acting in official duties, depredation response by designated employees, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to the taking prohibition — defense, agency actions, depredation response
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions include: (A) Any person may take a gray wolf in Minnesota in defense of his own life or the lives of others; (B) Designated employees/agents of the Service, other Federal land management agencies, or the Minnesota DNR may take wolves, without a permit, when acting in official duties to (1) aid a sick, injured, or orphaned specimen; (2) dispose of a dead specimen; or (3) salvage a dead specimen useful for scientific study; (C) Designated employees/agents may take a gray wolf in zones 2–5 in response to depredations on lawfully present domestic animals, provided such taking occurs within one-half mile of the depredation site, is performed in a humane manner, and any young-of-the-year taken on or before August 1 must be released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are narrowly defined, tied to agent designation and scope-of-duty, spatial and temporal limits (e.g., within 0.5 mile), and humane handling and release requirements. Regulatory drafters should include precise conditions for exceptions to avoid overbroad interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement for authorized takings (§17.40(d)(2)(i)(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any taking pursuant to the permitted exceptions must be reported by email to the Twin Cities Ecological Service Field Office at twincities@fws.gov within 5 days. The specimen may only be retained, disposed of, or salvaged in accordance with directions from the Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting timelines, contact method (email), and post-taking disposal/retention instructions must be specified in the rule so that authorized takers know immediate procedural obligations and chain-of-custody / scientific salvage requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permits — availability under §17.32 (General Permits—Threatened Wildlife)
rubrics_metrics.description: All permits available under §17.32 (General Permits—Threatened Wildlife) are available with regard to the gray wolf in Minnesota. All the terms and provisions of §17.32 apply to such permits issued under the authority of this paragraph (d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference existing general permit provisions rather than restating permit terms. Ensure that the rule explicitly states which existing permitting provisions apply and that permit issuance follows §17.32's terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export and commercial transaction prohibition (§17.40(d)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as may be authorized by a permit issued under §17.32, no person may sell or offer for sale in interstate commerce, import or export, or in the course of a commercial activity transport, ship, carry, deliver, or receive any Minnesota gray wolf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial and interstate trade prohibitions must be explicit with citation to permitting exceptions; this prevents unauthorized commerce and clarifies activities requiring permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on possession of unlawfully taken wolves (§17.40(d)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: No person may possess, sell, deliver, carry, transport, or ship, by any means whatsoever, a gray wolf taken unlawfully in Minnesota, except that designated employees/agents of the Service or other Federal land management agencies or the Minnesota DNR may, when acting in the course of official duties, possess, deliver, carry, transport, or ship a gray wolf taken unlawfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules must bar commerce and possession of unlawfully taken specimens while allowing agency personnel to handle such specimens in the course of official duties (e.g., evidence handling, salvage, research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical habitat designation (50 CFR 17.95(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The reinstated regulations at 50 CFR 17.95(a) designate critical habitat for gray wolf in Minnesota and Michigan (Isle Royale National Park and specified Minnesota counties with boundaries identical to zones 1–3 as delineated in 50 CFR 17.40(d)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical habitat entries must identify the geographic areas (counties, park units) and reference the regulatory zone definitions. Cross-references to zone descriptions ensure consistency between habitat and special rule boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope — list of states and portions affected
rubrics_metrics.description: As a result of the court order, gray wolves are listed as threatened in Minnesota and endangered in all or portions of 44 U.S. States and Mexico. The rule lists by name the States fully included and identifies portions of AZ, NM, OR, UT, and WA as depicted in figure 1 and the November 3, 2020 delisting rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules should explicitly enumerate affected States/areas to give regulated parties clear notice of where protections apply. The rule also explicitly notes exceptions (areas that remain delisted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Future actions — status review and proposed rule timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: By February 2, 2024, the Service intends to submit to the Office of the Federal Register a proposed rule concerning the listing status of gray wolves in the lower 48 United States under the Act. The status determination will be based on the best available information as of the time of publication. If the appeals proceed and the district court's order is reversed, the Service will take action to comply with and implement the Court of Appeals' judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rule is issued to comply with litigation, agencies should state planned follow-up rulemaking, the decision standard (best available information), and contingency plans if subsequent judicial developments require different action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority citation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority citation for part 17 continues to read as follows: Authority: 16 U.S.C. 1361-1407; 1531-1544; 4201-4245, unless otherwise noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory amendments must include the statutory authority citation that authorizes the agency to promulgate the rules; include correct U.S. Code citations for transparency and legal validity.
